Assume a car has a rated power of $80\mathrm{kW}$, a maximum speed of $20\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ on a flat road, and a mass of $2\times10^{3}\mathrm{kg}$. If the car starts from rest and undergoes uniformly accelerated linear motion with an acceleration of $2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, and the resistance remains constant during the motion.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: No image information is needed. Given rated power P_rated = 80 kW = 80000 W, maximum flat-road speed v_max = 20 m/s, mass m = 2.0 × 10^3 kg, initial uniform acceleration a = 2 m/s^2, and constant resistance. At maximum speed on a flat road, acceleration is zero, so the rated engine power balances resistance: f = P_rated / v_max = 80000 / 20 = 4000 N. During the initial uniformly accelerated stage, the required tractive force is F = ma + f = 2000 × 2 + 4000 = 8000 N. In this stage, engine power is P = Fv. The uniform-acceleration stage ends when P reaches the rated power: v = 80000 / 8000 = 10 m/s, so t = v / a = 10 / 2 = 5 s. At the end of the 3rd second, v = at = 2 × 3 = 6 m/s, so P = Fv = 8000 × 6 = 48000 W = 48 kW. When v = 16 m/s, the car is in the rated-power stage, so traction force is F = P_rated / v = 80000 / 16 = 5000 N. The net force is 5000 - 4000 = 1000 N, giving acceleration a = 1000 / 2000 = 0.5 m/s^2.

method.method_draft: Use a force-balance, two-regime dynamics route. From the text read rated power 80 kW, maximum flat-road speed 20 m/s, mass 2.0e3 kg, initial uniform acceleration 2 m/s^2, and constant resistance. No image information is needed. First, at maximum speed on a flat road the car is no longer accelerating, so the engine at rated power just balances resistance: f = P_rated / v_max = 80000/20 = 4000 N. During the initial uniformly accelerated stage, Newton's second law gives the required tractive force F = ma + f = 2000*2 + 4000 = 8000 N. The engine power in this stage is P = Fv, so the uniform-acceleration stage ends when Fv reaches 80 kW: v = 80000/8000 = 10 m/s, hence t = v/a = 10/2 = 5 s. At the end of the 3rd second, v = at = 6 m/s, so instantaneous power is P = Fv = 8000*6 = 48000 W = 48 kW. For v = 16 m/s, the car must be in the rated-power stage, so traction force is F = P_rated/v = 80000/16 = 5000 N; net force is 5000 - 4000 = 1000 N, giving acceleration a = 1000/2000 = 0.5 m/s^2.

method.method_draft: Use a power-time and power-balance route, minimizing explicit tractive-force reasoning. From the text read P_rated = 80 kW, v_max = 20 m/s, m = 2.0e3 kg, initial acceleration a0 = 2 m/s^2, and constant resistance. No image information is needed. Determine resistance from the rated-power terminal condition: at maximum speed, all engine power is spent against resistance, so f v_max = P_rated and f = 4000 N. During uniform acceleration, the rate of increase of kinetic energy plus the rate of work against resistance equals engine power: P(t) = d(1/2 mv^2)/dt + fv = mav + fv = (ma + f)v. Since v = a0 t, P(t) = (ma0 + f)a0 t. Set P(t)=80 kW to get the duration of uniform acceleration: t = 80000/[(2000*2 + 4000)*2] = 5 s. At t=3 s, use the same power-time formula: P(3)= (2000*2 + 4000)*(2*3)=48000 W=48 kW. For v=16 m/s, use the net power balance directly: rated power minus resistive power becomes kinetic-energy growth, so P_rated - fv = mav. Thus a = [80000 - 4000*16]/(2000*16)=0.5 m/s^2.

No image information is needed. Given P_rated = 80 kW = 80000 W, v_max = 20 m/s, m = 2.0e3 kg, uniform acceleration a0 = 2 m/s^2, and constant resistance f.

1. At maximum speed on a flat road, acceleration is zero, so all rated power is used to overcome resistance: f v_max = P_rated. Thus f = 80000 / 20 = 4000 N.

2. During the uniformly accelerated stage, use the power balance: engine power equals the rate of kinetic energy increase plus the rate of work against resistance. So P(t) = d(1/2 m v^2)/dt + f v = m a0 v + f v = (m a0 + f)v. Since v = a0 t, P(t) = (m a0 + f)a0 t. Substitute values: P(t) = (2000*2 + 4000)*2*t = 16000t W. The uniform acceleration ends when the power reaches the rated power: 16000t = 80000, so t = 5 s.

3. At the end of the 3rd second, t = 3 s, still within the uniform acceleration stage. P(3) = 16000*3 = 48000 W = 48 kW.

4. When v = 16 m/s, the car is in the constant rated power stage because the uniform acceleration stage ended at v = a0*t = 2*5 = 10 m/s. Use the net power balance: P_rated - f v = m a v. Thus a = (80000 - 4000*16)/(2000*16) = 16000/32000 = 0.5 m/s^2.
